# 1 Enoch Chapter 80 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn-astr (Aramaic) | **Section:** Astronomical Book (Book of Luminaries)

---

**80:1** And in those days the angel Uriel answered and said to me: Behold, I have shown you everything, Enoch, and I have revealed all things to you that you should see — this sun and this moon, and the leaders of the stars of heaven and all those who turn them, their tasks and times and departures.

**80:2** And in the days of the sinners the years shall be shortened, and their seed shall be tardy on their lands and fields, and all things on the earth shall alter and shall not appear in their time; and the rain shall be kept back and the heaven shall withhold it.

**80:3** And in those times the fruits of the earth shall be backward and shall not grow in their time, and the fruits of the trees shall be withheld in their time.

**80:4** And the moon shall alter her order and not appear at her time.

**80:5** And in those days the sun shall be seen journeying in the evening on the extremity of the great chariot in the west, and shall shine more brightly than accords with the order of light.

**80:6** And many chiefs of the stars shall transgress the order prescribed to them, and these shall alter their orbits and tasks, and not appear at the seasons prescribed to them.

**80:7** And the whole order of the stars shall be concealed from the sinners, and the thoughts of those on the earth shall err concerning them, and they shall be altered from all their ways — yea, they shall err and take them to be gods.

**80:8** And evil shall be multiplied upon them, and punishment shall come upon them so as to destroy all.

---

*SOPHIA notes: Consensus rendering adjudicated from EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA. Chapter 80 is the eschatological disruption of the cosmic order established in chs. 72-79. In the end times: years are shortened (v. 2), harvests fail (vv. 2-3), the moon deviates (v. 4), the sun brightens abnormally (v. 5), stars abandon their courses (v. 6), and the ultimate consequence is astral idolatry (v. 7). This represents the theological stakes of the calendar dispute: wrong reckoning leads to worship of the wrong things.*
